title: The changing state in Country P
body: Country P, a developing country, opened its economy to foreign investment fifteen years ago. Since then it has sold several state-run enterprises, reduced subsidies on some public services and allowed private firms, including multinational companies, to decide where many new hospitals and schools are built. Economic and social priorities are now set largely by the market. At the same time, the government has introduced a digital identity system that links each citizen's bank account, tax record and mobile phone number, which helps it track tax evasion and transfer benefits directly. Its army and police remain fully under national control, and it continues to compete with a neighbouring country over a disputed border.
